text: Is it not a pleasure to learn and put what you learn into practice?
Review what you have learned and discover something new; then you can be a teacher.
Among any three people walking together, I can always find someone to learn from.
Knowing is not as good as loving to learn; loving to learn is not as good as finding joy in it.
Keep carving without giving up, and even metal and stone can be engraved.
Without gathering small streams, there can be no rivers or seas.
Learn widely, question carefully, think deeply, distinguish clearly, and act earnestly.
source: Book of Rites, Doctrine of the Mean

text: Renew yourself today, renew yourself each day, and keep renewing yourself.
A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath your feet.
Act before trouble takes shape; put things in order before disorder begins.
Understanding others is wisdom; understanding yourself is clarity.
As heaven moves with enduring strength, strive ceaselessly to improve yourself.
source: Book of Changes, Qian: The Image

text: As the earth bears all things, cultivate the generosity to embrace them.
source: Book of Changes, Kun: The Image

text: Walk to where the stream ends, then sit and watch the clouds rise.
Beyond winding mountains and streams, where the path seems lost, a village appears among willows and flowers.
source: Visiting a Village West of the Mountains

text: The day will come to ride the wind and break the waves; I will raise my sail and cross the open sea.
The welcome rain knows its season and arrives when spring begins.
source: Delight in Rain on a Spring Night

text: One day I will reach the highest summit and see all the mountains below.
To see a thousand miles farther, climb one more floor.
Let the rain beat through the woods and leaves; I will sing and walk at ease.
source: Ding Feng Bo: Rain Through the Woods

text: Is it not a joy to welcome friends from afar?
Be diligent in action and careful in speech; seek those with principles to guide you.
When you see goodness, aspire to it; when you see faults, examine yourself.
Be eager to learn, and never be ashamed to ask someone of lower standing.
As you seek to establish yourself, help others do the same; as you seek to advance, help others advance.
Never tire of learning, and never grow weary of teaching.
Help others bring their good intentions to fruition, and do not further their wrongs.
To do good work, first sharpen your tools.
When kindness calls, do not hold back, even in deference to your teacher.
Friendship with the upright, the trustworthy, and the well-informed brings benefit.
Learn widely with firm purpose, ask earnestly, and reflect on what is near at hand; kindness is found within these things.
Make friends through learning, and let friendship help you cultivate kindness.
Care for your elders and extend that care to others' elders; cherish your children and extend that care to others' children.
Those who rejoice in the people's happiness will find the people rejoicing in theirs.
There is no greater good than helping others do what is right.
Everyone can aspire to the goodness of Yao and Shun.
The kindhearted love others; the courteous respect others.
Those who love others are loved in return; those who respect others are respected in return.
Look up without shame before heaven, and look around without shame before others.
Begin with affection for family, extend kindness to people, and extend care to all living things.
Indigo comes from the blue plant, yet its color is deeper than the plant's own.
Learn widely and examine yourself each day; your understanding will grow clear and your conduct more sound.
A whole day spent thinking alone cannot match even a brief time spent learning.
The cultivated person has no different nature, but knows how to make good use of what is available.
Gather earth into a mountain, and wind and rain arise; gather water into a deep pool, and dragons dwell there.
Without adding up small steps, you cannot travel a thousand miles.
Even a short road must be walked; even a small task must be done.
Hearing is not as good as seeing; seeing is not as good as understanding; understanding is not as good as doing.
Jade must be carved to become a fine object; people must learn to understand the Way.
source: Book of Rites, Record of Learning

text: Learning reveals what you lack; teaching reveals what you have yet to understand.
source: Book of Rites, Record of Learning

text: Recognizing what you lack invites reflection; recognizing your difficulties inspires further effort.
source: Book of Rites, Record of Learning

text: A fine singer inspires others to continue the song; a fine teacher inspires others to carry on the purpose.
source: Book of Rites, Record of Learning

text: Guide without dragging, encourage without pressing, and open the way without supplying every answer.
source: Book of Rites, Record of Learning

text: Things have roots and branches; actions have beginnings and endings. Understanding their order brings you closer to the Way.
All things grow together without harming one another; different paths proceed without conflict.
source: Book of Rites, Doctrine of the Mean

text: Great learning means bringing virtue to light, caring for the people, and resting in the highest good.
The highest goodness is like water: it benefits all things without competing.
In learning, add something each day; in following the Way, let something go each day.
Overcoming others takes force; overcoming yourself takes strength.
Great perfection seems unfinished, yet its use never wears out; great fullness seems empty, yet its use never runs dry.
Difficult tasks begin with easy steps; great undertakings begin with small details.
A tree that fills your arms grows from a tiny shoot; a nine-story terrace begins with a heap of earth.
Be as careful at the end as at the beginning, and your work will not fail.
When you see goodness, follow it; when you find a fault, correct it.
source: Book of Changes, Yi: The Image

text: Two people united in purpose can cut through metal; words from united hearts are fragrant as orchids.
source: Book of Changes, Great Commentary I

text: Learn through discussion and practice with friends.
source: Book of Changes, Dui: The Image

text: At an impasse, change; through change, find a way forward; through that opening, endure.
source: Book of Changes, Great Commentary II

text: Learn widely from the words and deeds of the past to nurture your character.
source: Book of Changes, Da Xu: The Image

text: Cultivate yourself through calm, and nurture character through simplicity.
Simplicity makes purpose clear; calm allows you to reach far.
Bright moonlight shines between the pines; a clear spring flows over stones.
Returning sunlight enters the deep woods and shines again upon the green moss.
Alone among quiet bamboo, I play my zither and sing. Unseen in the deep woods, I have the bright moon for company.
Pink peach blossoms still hold last night's rain; green willows wear the morning mist.
White egrets fly over broad flooded fields; golden orioles sing in the shade of summer trees.
Green trees gather around the village; blue hills stretch beyond its walls.
An old friend prepares chicken and millet, inviting me to his country home.
Before the cries of apes on both banks have faded, my light boat has passed countless mountains.
source: Leaving White Emperor City at Dawn

text: Green mountains rise on either bank; a lone sail comes from the edge of the sun.
At dawn I leave White Emperor City among colored clouds; distant Jiangling is reached within a day.
source: Leaving White Emperor City at Dawn

text: At rest, I notice osmanthus blossoms fall; the night is still and the spring hills quiet.
url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/皇甫嶽雲溪雜題五首/鳥鳴澗

text: In spring sleep I miss the dawn; birdsong reaches me from everywhere.
Long spring days brighten hills and rivers; the breeze carries flowers' scent. Swallows fly over soft earth; ducks sleep on warm sand.
I delight in these famous mountains; looking upon them, my heart grows calmer.
source: Gazing at the Waterfalls of Mount Lu, No. 1

text: Two golden orioles sing among green willows; a line of white egrets rises into the blue sky.
Playful butterflies linger in their dance; carefree orioles sing their sweet notes.
source: Seeking Flowers Alone by the River, No. 6

text: A cluster of peach blossoms blooms for no one in particular, deep red lovely beside pale red.
source: Seeking Flowers Alone by the River, No. 5

text: The rain slips into the night with the wind, quietly nourishing everything.
source: Delight in Rain on a Spring Night

text: Early orioles compete for sunlit trees; new swallows gather the spring mud.
source: A Spring Walk by Qiantang Lake

text: Fresh wine foams green beside a small red-clay stove. Snow is coming this evening; will you share a cup?
When April's blossoms have faded below, the mountain temple's peach trees are just coming into bloom.
A fine rain softens the city streets; grass looks green from afar, yet vanishes when seen close by.
source: Early Spring: To Zhang of the Water Department, No. 1
url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/早春呈水部張十八員外二首

text: A crane rises through clouds in the clear sky, carrying my thoughts toward poetry and the blue heights.
From afar, Dongting's hills and waters shine green: a blue-green snail upon a silver plate.
At full tide the river opens wide; a fair wind lifts the sail. The sun rises before night has gone, and spring arrives before the old year ends.
Trees and grasses know spring will soon depart, and vie in shades of red and purple.
A tall willow dressed in jade lets down ten thousand green ribbons. Who cut its slender leaves? The spring wind, sharp as scissors.
A spring quietly releases its slender stream; tree shade rests on sunlit water. A lotus tip has just appeared, and a dragonfly already perches there.
Lotus leaves stretch green to the sky's edge; sunlit lotus blossoms glow a red all their own.
source: Leaving Jingci Temple at Dawn to See Lin Zifang Off

text: A child runs after a yellow butterfly, which flies into the rapeseed flowers and disappears.
source: Staying at Mr. Xu's Inn in Xinshi

text: The east wind's presence is easy to recognize: the countless reds and purples are all spring.
A small square pond opens like a mirror, holding sky and passing clouds. Why is it so clear? Fresh water keeps flowing from its source.
The thrush moves freely through a thousand notes, among red and purple mountain flowers and trees of every height.
The lake sparkles beautifully in sunlight; the misty mountains are just as wondrous in rain.
source: Drinking by the Lake After Sunshine and Rain, No. 2

text: A few peach branches bloom beyond the bamboo; ducks are first to feel the spring river's warmth.
source: On Huichong's Evening Scene of a Spring River

text: Remember the year's finest season: when oranges turn golden and tangerines remain green.
The green shade is as deep as on the outward road, now joined by four or five oriole calls.
A few plum branches bloom alone in the cold beside the wall. From afar I know it is not snow: a subtle fragrance reaches me.
Clouds are light and the breeze gentle near noon; past flowers and willows, I cross the stream ahead.
Young orchid shoots dip into the stream below the hill; the sandy path among the pines is clean of mud.
source: Huan Xi Sha: Visiting Qingquan Temple
url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/浣溪沙（遊蘄水清泉寺，寺臨蘭溪，溪水西流）

text: Let a fresh fire brew this season's tea; enjoy poetry and wine while the days are yours.
source: Wang Jiang Nan: At Chaoran Terrace

text: Before me: a zither, a pot of wine, and a stream of clouds.
The children do not yet know farming or weaving, but learn to plant melons in the mulberry shade.
White tea foam floats in the noon cup; tender herbs fill the spring plate. Life's finest flavor is simple contentment.
source: Huan Xi Sha: A Chilly Morning of Slanting Rain
url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/浣溪沙（元豐七年十月二十四日，從泗州劉倩叔遊南山）

text: Returning late by boat, we stray deep among lotus flowers. Row on, row on! A whole shore of gulls and egrets takes flight.
source: Ru Meng Ling: Remembering Dusk at the Stream Pavilion
url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/如夢令_(李清照)/如夢令_(常記溪亭日暮)

text: White egrets fly before Xisai Mountain; peach blossoms drift where perch grow fat. In bamboo hat and green raincoat, I need not leave this gentle rain.
source: Yu Ge Zi: Egrets Before Xisai Mountain

text: With bamboo staff and straw sandals, I move more lightly than on horseback. Why fear? A raincoat is enough for a lifetime of mist and rain.
source: Ding Feng Bo: Rain Through the Woods

text: The scent of rice flowers promises a rich harvest; listen to the chorus of frogs.
source: Xi Jiang Yue: A Night Walk Along Huangsha Road

text: Who says life cannot feel young again? The stream before the gate still flows west.
source: Huan Xi Sha: Visiting Qingquan Temple
url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/浣溪沙（遊蘄水清泉寺，寺臨蘭溪，溪水西流）

text: At sunrise, riverside flowers glow redder than fire; in spring, the river shines green as indigo.
source: Remembering the South: The South Is Beautiful
